plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of two nested surfaces over a labeled coordinate frame, with the x axis coming forward to the lower left, the y axis running right, and the z axis vertical. The outer surface is a downward-opening paraboloid drawn as a translucent shell shaded in blue and salmon; its apex sits on the z axis at the marked point (0, 0, 2), and it widens as it descends, closing in a broad elliptical rim near the xy-plane. Nested inside is a cone with its vertex at the origin, opening upward and shaded darker blue-gray, its circular top rim appearing as an ellipse partway up the paraboloid's interior. Two horizontal arrows carry the equations: the left arrow points to the inner cone and reads z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), the right arrow points to the outer shell and reads z = 2 - x^2 - y^2. Dashed segments trace the hidden part of the z axis and the far side of the base rim. Nesting one surface inside the other makes the enclosed solid legible, with a curved dome above and a pointed conical floor below. The sketch fixes the region whose volume is to be set up as a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates.

elements: z-axis vertical with arrowhead and label 'z' at top
y-axis horizontal to the right with arrowhead and label 'y'
x-axis receding to the lower-left (toward viewer) with arrowhead and label 'x'
dashed hidden portion of the z-axis below the apex and dashed far side of the paraboloid base rim

outer downward-opening paraboloid z = 2 - x^2 - y^2 as a translucent shell (blue with salmon shading), apex on z-axis at (0,0,2), widening to a broad elliptical base rim near the xy-plane at r = sqrt(2)
apex point marker with label '(0, 0, 2)' beside the top of the z-axis
inner upward-opening cone z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2) as a translucent darker blue-gray surface, vertex at the origin, circular rim at the intersection z = 1, r = 1
intersection circle (r = 1, z = 1) where cone meets paraboloid, drawn as a highlighted ring
left horizontal arrow pointing right at the cone carrying the equation label
right horizontal arrow pointing left at the paraboloid carrying the equation label
radial base line in the xy-plane from the origin to (r, theta, 0)
vertical segment at azimuth theta from the cone surface z = r up to the paraboloid surface z = 2 - r^2, with endpoint dots
optional radial-symmetry highlight (faint radial spokes / translucent ring) shown in cylindrical mode

interactions.teaches: Rotating the nested surfaces reveals that the cone forms a pointed floor and the paraboloid a curved dome, so the enclosed solid is bounded below by the cone and above by the paraboloid

interactions.label: Radial coordinate r
interactions.teaches: Sweeping r outward from the z-axis moves a vertical segment whose bottom rides the cone (z = r) and top rides the paraboloid (z = 2 - r^2); the segment shrinks to zero at r = 1 where the surfaces meet, showing exactly why the cylindrical z-bounds run from the cone up to the paraboloid over r in [0,1]

interactions.label: Coordinate form
interactions.teaches: Switching the surface labels from z = sqrt(x^2+y^2), z = 2 - x^2 - y^2 to z = r, z = 2 - r^2 (with a radial-symmetry highlight) makes clear that both surfaces depend only on r, which is why cylindrical coordinates collapse the setup to simple r and z bounds

demo_steps.title: Nested surfaces (Cartesian)
demo_steps.narration: The translucent paraboloid z = 2 - x^2 - y^2 (apex (0,0,2)) encloses the upward cone z = sqrt(x^2+y^2); their intersection is the ring at r = 1, z = 1. The radial segment at r = 0.5 spans from the cone up to the paraboloid.

demo_steps.title: Sweep r to the intersection
demo_steps.narration: Drag r toward 1: the segment's bottom (cone) rises and its top (paraboloid) falls until they coincide at z = 1, r = 1 — the radial extent of the solid is exactly 0 <= r <= 1.

demo_steps.title: Cylindrical form
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to cylindrical: the labels become z = r and z = 2 - r^2 and a radial-symmetry highlight appears, exposing that each surface is a function of r alone, so the volume integral uses z from r to 2 - r^2 and r from 0 to 1.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units: paraboloid z = 2 - r^2 spans r in [0, sqrt(2)] (~1.414) at z=0 with apex (0,0,2); cone z = r drawn from vertex (0,0,0) to rim (r=1, z=1); intersection ring at r=1, z=1. Build both as lathe/parametric surfaces, double-sided, transparent. Axes: +z up, +y screen-right, +x toward lower-left (viewer); arrowheads + labels x,y,z in black. Apex label '(0,0,2)' offset right of z-axis top. Left equation arrow on the left pointing right at the cone; right equation arrow on the right pointing left at the paraboloid. Radial segment fixed azimuth theta ~ 45 deg (world, toward +x+y so it reads in front): bottom dot at (r cos, r sin, r), top dot at (r cos, r sin, 2-r^2), plus base line origin->(r cos, r sin, 0). Colors: paraboloid translucent blue #6fa8dc blended with salmon #e8a08a; cone translucent slate #5a6b8c; intersection ring orange #ff7a00; radial segment red #d22; axes/labels black #111. Key math: surfaces meet where r = 2 - r^2 -> r = 1, z = 1; paraboloid base at r = sqrt(2).
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE LatheGeometry (or custom BufferGeometry) for both surfaces with MeshBasicMaterial/MeshPhongMaterial transparent (opacity ~0.45) and side: DoubleSide so the nesting reads. Recompute the radial segment endpoints, base line, and endpoint spheres reactively on every slider change; clamp r to [0,1]. For the cylindrical toggle, swap the two label strings and fade in a radial-symmetry highlight (e.g. 8 faint radial spokes on the cone/paraboloid or a translucent annulus at z=1) via show/hide rather than rebuilding geometry. Keep dashed lines (hidden z-axis, far base rim) as LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances().

authoredContext:
Let E be the region bounded below by the cone z=x2+y2 and above by the paraboloid z=2−x2−y2. (the figure). Set up a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates to find the volume of the region, using the following orders of integration:

Setting up a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates over a conical region.

A paraboloid with equation z = 2 minus x squared minus y squared opening down, and within it, a cone with equation z = the square root of (x squared + y squared) pointing down.

Two horizontal arrows carry the equations: the left arrow points to the inner cone and reads z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), the right arrow points to the outer shell and reads z = 2 - x^2 - y^2. Dashed segments trace the hidden part of the z axis and the far side of the base rim. Nesting one surface inside the other makes the enclosed solid legible, with a curved dome above and a pointed conical floor below. The sketch fixes the region whose volume is to be set up as a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates.

interactions.teaches: Rotating the nested surfaces reveals that the cone forms a pointed floor and the paraboloid a curved dome, so the enclosed solid is bounded below by the cone and above by the paraboloid

interactions.label: Radial coordinate r
interactions.teaches: Sweeping r outward from the z-axis moves a vertical segment whose bottom rides the cone (z = r) and top rides the paraboloid (z = 2 - r^2); the segment shrinks to zero at r = 1 where the surfaces meet, showing exactly why the cylindrical z-bounds run from the cone up to the paraboloid over r in [0,1]

interactions.label: Coordinate form
interactions.teaches: Switching the surface labels from z = sqrt(x^2+y^2), z = 2 - x^2 - y^2 to z = r, z = 2 - r^2 (with a radial-symmetry highlight) makes clear that both surfaces depend only on r, which is why cylindrical coordinates collapse the setup to simple r and z bounds

demo_steps.title: Nested surfaces (Cartesian)
demo_steps.narration: The translucent paraboloid z = 2 - x^2 - y^2 (apex (0,0,2)) encloses the upward cone z = sqrt(x^2+y^2); their intersection is the ring at r = 1, z = 1. The radial segment at r = 0.5 spans from the cone up to the paraboloid.

demo_steps.title: Sweep r to the intersection
demo_steps.narration: Drag r toward 1: the segment's bottom (cone) rises and its top (paraboloid) falls until they coincide at z = 1, r = 1 — the radial extent of the solid is exactly 0 <= r <= 1.

demo_steps.title: Cylindrical form
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to cylindrical: the labels become z = r and z = 2 - r^2 and a radial-symmetry highlight appears, exposing that each surface is a function of r alone, so the volume integral uses z from r to 2 - r^2 and r from 0 to 1.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units: paraboloid z = 2 - r^2 spans r in [0, sqrt(2)] (~1.414) at z=0 with apex (0,0,2); cone z = r drawn from vertex (0,0,0) to rim (r=1, z=1); intersection ring at r=1, z=1. Build both as lathe/parametric surfaces, double-sided, transparent. Axes: +z up, +y screen-right, +x toward lower-left (viewer); arrowheads + labels x,y,z in black. Apex label '(0,0,2)' offset right of z-axis top. Left equation arrow on the left pointing right at the cone; right equation arrow on the right pointing left at the paraboloid. Radial segment fixed azimuth theta ~ 45 deg (world, toward +x+y so it reads in front): bottom dot at (r cos, r sin, r), top dot at (r cos, r sin, 2-r^2), plus base line origin->(r cos, r sin, 0). Colors: paraboloid translucent blue #6fa8dc blended with salmon #e8a08a; cone translucent slate #5a6b8c; intersection ring orange #ff7a00; radial segment red #d22; axes/labels black #111. Key math: surfaces meet where r = 2 - r^2 -> r = 1, z = 1; paraboloid base at r = sqrt(2).
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE LatheGeometry (or custom BufferGeometry) for both surfaces with MeshBasicMaterial/MeshPhongMaterial transparent (opacity ~0.45) and side: DoubleSide so the nesting reads. Recompute the radial segment endpoints, base line, and endpoint spheres reactively on every slider change; clamp r to [0,1]. For the cylindrical toggle, swap the two label strings and fade in a radial-symmetry highlight (e.g. 8 faint radial spokes on the cone/paraboloid or a translucent annulus at z=1) via show/hide rather than rebuilding geometry. Keep dashed lines (hidden z-axis, far base rim) as LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances().
